close_reason: Strengthened assert_extras_roundtrip's assertion from back[vendor_key] == vendor_val to full back == raw. Preserved the (raw, vendor_key, vendor_val) signature so all 27 call sites need no change (option 1 of the two paths I considered; option 2 was the bead's suggestion of also simplifying the signature to (raw_with_vendor), which is mostly aesthetic since the safety benefit lands either way). Added a doc-comment on the helper explaining the flatten+rename bug class it now catches. All 59 tests pass — the strengthened helper found no pre-existing regression. Commit pending.
description: lib.rs:1581-1595 defines assert_extras_roundtrip<T>, which mutates the input value to inject a vendor field, deserializes, re-serializes, and asserts ONLY that back[vendor_key] equals vendor_val. Compare assert_roundtrip at :1172-1180 which asserts full back == value. The weaker helper is used by 27 extras-preservation tests. If serde flatten + rename had a subtle interaction that caused a typed field to land in extras or vice versa, the extras tests would not catch it (the round-trip tests at :1184-1554 would, but only for inputs without a vendor field). Suggested rewrite: change assert_extras_roundtrip to assert back == raw (after the mutation), matching assert_roundtrip's strength. The vendor_key/vendor_val arguments become redundant once the assertion is full-equality, so the helper could be simplified to assert_extras_roundtrip<T>(raw_with_vendor: Value).
title: assert_extras_roundtrip helper checks only the vendor key, not full object equality
